trigger.review: First execution of build-fimm-exploratory-results against the real Roihu sources, 2026-09-29
trigger.defect: The legacy FIMM cross-modality analysis predates PanelHLA and pairs specimens by allele fingerprint, so it cannot estimate cross-modality agreement.

cross_modality_caller_agreement.detail: The merged workbook has 2642 data rows and exactly eight columns: Method, Seq_type, HLA_A_1, HLA_A_2, HLA_B_1, HLA_B_2, HLA_C_1, HLA_C_2. There is no sample identifier column, so analyze_fimm_hla.py matched scRNA specimens to bulk RNA and WES specimens by allele fingerprint and then scored those pairs for HLA concordance.
observed_consequences: arcasHLA on scRNA versus arcasHLA on bulk RNA and on WES both reported 35 of 35, a trivial self-agreement
tier A scRNA versus bulk RNA, split by the scRNA caller panel: arcashla 21 of 21, arcashla plus optitype 75 of 84, optitype-only 0 of 33
the optitype-only stratum disagreeing at every locus dragged the pooled tier A estimate from 0.893 to 0.696

wes_allele_imbalance_category.detail: All 225 rows of fimm_spechla_freq_wes_deident.tsv carry het_variant_count 0 and major_allele_fraction 1.0, so every donor-locus record classified as excluded_nonheterozygous (207) or insufficient (18) and no informative category existed. The RNA counterpart carries real frequencies but its own modality_caveat column excludes it from loss-of-heterozygosity classification because it measures differential expression rather than copy number.

bb72_serogroup_agreement.reason: Linkage is by specimen identity, not by allele similarity. validate_hla_a2_flow.py derives a donor key from the sample identifier and joins flow records to sequenced specimens on that key, so the endpoint is not circular.
bb72_serogroup_agreement.mandatory_reporting: Every estimate must be reported with its linkage fraction and unlinked counts: 16 of 53 flow donors linked, informative counts 8 scRNA, 14 bulk RNA, 13 WES, linkage fractions 0.151 to 0.264.

additional_finding_not_a_defect.no_disjoint_caller_contrast: Caller panels in the legacy FIMM tables are scRNA {arcashla, optitype} and bulk RNA equal to WES {arcashla, optitype, spechla}. Every panel intersection equals the smaller panel, so no caller is unique to any assay and no caller-disjoint contrast exists. Recorded because it constrains what any future FIMM cross-modality endpoint can mean, independently of the circularity above.

replacement_analysis: Per-caller HLA predictions carrying an explicit per-sample identifier are run through the PanelHLA consensus path (champhla_confirmation.consensus.build_consensus) over the declared panels. Specimen and donor linkage come from the sample registry or from the donor_key resolver, never from allele content.
retention_rule: This withdrawal stands regardless of whether a corrected analysis would be more or less favourable to the manuscript.
